clue.text: Report covering achievement, having abandoned a refuge

indicators.note: one piece wraps around the other, as a cover goes over something

parts.note: to report something is to say it

indicators.note: the achievement word has dropped the clue's 'a', as if leaving it behind

parts.note: a feat is a notable achievement

explanation.surface: A news report on someone's accomplishment, after they have left a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having abandoned a' removes the A from the achievement word; 'covering' wraps the report word around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of protection from danger, which is what safety means in phrases like 'reach safety'.

clue.text: Air circulating on jumbo jets all finally used up

indicators.note: in a down clue, letters read upwards come out backwards
the last letter of each of the words before 'all' is taken, as 'all finally' says

explanation.surface: Air circulating through big passenger planes is all spent by the end of the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all finally' takes the last letters G, N, O, S of four words; 'used up' reverses them, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, so a piece that is sung fits the sense.

clue.text: Suggestion: somewhere to go in all seasons

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: there are four seasons in a year
a lav (lavatory) is somewhere one goes, in the toilet sense

explanation.surface: A recommendation for a destination that suits every time of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhere to go' looks like a holiday spot but means the toilet, a British euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavour of something is a hint or trace of it, much as a suggestion is.

clue.text: Source of news then oddly allowed after, not leader

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word then are taken

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for after is dropped

parts.note: next means coming after

explanation.surface: A news source that was then strangely permitted, once it had lost its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not leader' strips N from NEXT, leaving EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Teletext was a television text service carrying news headlines and other information pages.

clue.text: Firing weapon, one flying straight over ship, then boat cut in half

indicators.note: the bird word goes over and around the other letters

parts.note: the crow is said to fly in a straight line, as in 'as the crow flies'
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: only the first half of the word boat is kept

explanation.surface: A weapon fired from a bird skimming over a ship, followed by a boat sliced in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one flying straight' is the bird from the phrase 'as the crow flies'; 'cut in half' keeps the first half of boat, and 'over' wraps the bird around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbow is a mechanical bow that shoots bolts, so it is a weapon that is fired.

clue.text: Review of short play in theatre adaptation?

indicators.note: to review is to look again and revise, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic's write-up of a brief drama in a stage version.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre is the operating theatre, not the stage: the adaptation is a surgical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinoplasty is cosmetic surgery to reshape the nose, an alteration done in an operating theatre.

clue.text: Slump that was painful after gutting of sawmill

indicators.note: the cry comes after the letters from the mill
removing the insides of the word sawmill leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: ouch is what someone says when something hurts

explanation.surface: A downturn at a sawmill, where it hurt to have the place stripped out.
explanation.definitionFit: To slouch is to slump, sitting or standing in a lazy drooping way.

clue.text: Top row of vehicles?

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: The upper deck of a line of vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: A row of vehicles reads as a bus tier, with 'of' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustier is a close-fitting strapless garment worn as a top.

clue.text: Shower mat slipping on top of that

indicators.note: a mat that slips slides out of place, so the letters are moved

explanation.surface: A bath mat sliding about, and as if that were not enough...
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms that add one more point to what has already been said, like 'besides'.

clue.text: Not quite noon, expected later

parts.note: something early comes before it was expected, so it was expected later

explanation.surface: It is almost midday, with something due to arrive afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expected later' is a cryptic take on early: what arrives early was expected at a later time.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost, falling just short, which is not quite.

clue.text: Brief hint: solver needs answer that's "water off Australia"

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the hint word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tip is a hint
Inspector Morse is the fictional detective who solves crimes in Oxford

explanation.surface: A crossword hint telling the solver the answer is a body of water near Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' trims TIP to TI. The solver is not the person doing the puzzle but Inspector Morse, the TV detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The Timor Sea lies between northern Australia and the island of Timor, a stretch of ocean off the coast.

clue.text: Short script edited with info and photo that's traditionally found in newspaper

indicators.note: editing rearranges material, so the letters are reworked
short means cut, so the word script loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A trimmed text revised with information and a picture, the sort of thing printed in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the script word before 'edited' mixes the letters with the other two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish-and-chip shops in Britain traditionally wrapped their chips in old newspaper.

clue.text: Beastly sound arising, father's about to threaten diminutive figure

indicators.note: in a down clue, letters rising read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: moo is the sound a cow makes

indicators.note: the father letters go around the threat word

parts.note: read as father is, father appears twice: pa and pa
to loom is to threaten, as a storm looms

explanation.surface: A cow lowing as a parent is on the point of menacing a little person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' reverses the cow's sound, as this is a down entry; 'father's' is read as father twice, which 'about' puts around the threat word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oompa-Loompas are the tiny workers in Roald Dahl's Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

clue.text: Backing of king sufficient, say

indicators.note: backing means turning backwards, applied to the word of

parts.note: rex is Latin for king
ample means enough

explanation.surface: Support from a monarch is enough, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support but reverses OF to FO; only 'of' is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Say can introduce an illustration, as in 'take a city, say Paris', which is what the phrase does.

clue.text: Spanish Steps short of energy dry up — entertainment, barely?

indicators.note: lacking, so the energy letters are removed

parts.note: the fandango is a lively Spanish dance
go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read backwards

parts.note: sec is the wine term for dry

explanation.surface: The famous Rome landmark, out of puff, drying up, as a scanty sort of show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish Steps are not the Rome landmark but a Spanish dance. 'short of energy' removes GO from FANDANGO; 'up' turns SEC into CES.
explanation.definitionFit: Fan dances are burlesque routines where a nearly nude dancer is covered only by fans.

clue.text: Accordingly caught by better goalkeeper

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words, held by them

explanation.surface: As a result, the shot was held by a superior keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean consequently.

clue.text: Clever lot, males promoted before relations

indicators.note: the sheep come before the connections
in a down clue, raising letters reads them upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rams are male sheep
ties are relations or connections

explanation.surface: A brainy group, with the men moved up ahead of their kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarties is a playful plural for smart people, clever clogs; it is also a British sweet.

clue.text: Pavilion ultimately remains — his design?

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word Pavilion is taken

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Only the end of the pavilion survives: was it his work?
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Pavilion in Brighton, an English seaside town, was designed by the architect John Nash.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark points to the architect who designed Brighton's Royal Pavilion; 'his' stands for that designer.

clue.text: Playwright born a Native American

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright
née marks a maiden name, meaning born

explanation.surface: A dramatist who was born a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are a Native American people originally from the Ohio Valley.

clue.text: Children's author admitting actions an online threat

indicators.note: letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote the children's classic Swallows and Amazons
military actions add up to war

explanation.surface: A writer for children confesses to deeds that pose an internet danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransomware is malicious software that locks a victim's files until a payment is made.

clue.text: Small vinegary drinks for abstainer, perhaps?

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: acetic means relating to vinegar

explanation.surface: Little sour drinks suit someone who avoids alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic practises severe self-denial; a teetotaller is one kind, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Complex put on private residential area

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so the letters are tangled

parts.note: own means personal or private, as in 'my own room'

explanation.surface: A housing complex put on a private estate in a residential district.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptown is the residential part of a city away from the business centre, mainly in American usage.

clue.text: Like track I see in English city, start of line from small village?

definitions.text: start of line from small village?

parts.note: à la means in the style of
spoor is an animal's track

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: York is a city in northern England
C is how the word see sounds

explanation.surface: Something like a trail I spot in a cathedral city, apparently from a village.
explanation.walkthrough: The small village is a hamlet, so Hamlet, Shakespeare's play. 'in' puts I and the letter for 'see' inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's speech over the jester's skull begins with these words, so they open a line from the play.

clue.text: Fair old pan having bottom scrubbed

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which is removed

parts.note: a pot is a cooking pan

explanation.surface: A decent old saucepan that has had its base cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having bottom scrubbed' removes the T at the foot of EXPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exhibition, and a fair in the trade-show sense is the same thing.

clue.text: Right battle it's clear

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, the party of the political right
the Somme was a First World War battle

explanation.surface: The right battle, it's obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup made from strained stock, so it is a clear thing.

clue.text: Announcement of written arrangement, a charge on smokers etc?

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken, so the word is said out

parts.note: syntax is the arrangement of words in written sentences

explanation.surface: Declaring a written plan for a levy on cigarettes and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin tax is a levy on goods seen as vices, such as tobacco and alcohol.

clue.text: Grand people in sweaty shifts

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Important people stuck in damp work periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' is the grand piano, and Steinway & Sons are the people who make them.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinway & Sons is a famous piano maker known for its concert grands.

clue.text: Film us leaving cat with tailless dog

indicators.note: the word us departs from the cat word

parts.note: puss or pussy is a cat
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the dog word is cut off

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: We walk out on a movie featuring a cat and a dog with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us leaving' removes US from PUSSY to leave PSY; 'tailless' trims CHOW to CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Alfred Hitchcock's 1960 thriller film.
